knowledge_base: Each refactoring step must keep the test suite green; if a step requires test changes, that is itself a step.
Prefer 'extract function' before 'rename' so the rename happens on a self-contained unit and is easier to revert.
Splitting a file at the 150-LOC limit usually starts by extracting the largest cohesive class, not by line count.
Cycles in the import graph are broken by introducing an interfaces.py shared by both ends, not by lazy imports.
Parameter-object refactor is justified when 3+ scalar arguments always travel together through 2+ call sites.
Mechanical renames are safe to do in one commit; semantic renames (changing meaning) should be split into two.
When extracting a method, copy the body first, then re-route call sites, then delete the original — never both at once.
Refactors that change public exports must update __all__, the SDK facade, and the docs in the same PR.
Reversibility matters: each step should have a one-line description of how to undo it via git revert of that commit.
Tools like libcst and rope produce safer renames than regex; prefer them when the rename touches more than 5 files.

templates.split_file: Split {file} ({loc} LOC) into {parts}; keep public API in {facade}.
templates.break_cycle: Move {shared} into {interfaces_module}; have {a} and {b} import from it only.
